title: Extension of partial disjoint-spectra plateaued families
summary: Determine whether every partial pairwise-disjoint family of nontrivial s-plateaued Boolean spectra can be completed to a family of size 2^s.

formal_statement.body: Let $f_1,...,f_r$ be nontrivial $s$-plateaued Boolean functions on $F_2^n$ with pairwise disjoint Walsh spectra and $r<2^s$. Must there always exist $s$-plateaued functions $f_{r+1},...,f_{2^s}$ such that the full family has pairwise disjoint spectra? Prove this for every admissible partial family or exhibit one admissible nonextendable family.

scope.domain: Plateaued Boolean functions, Walsh spectra, and disjoint-spectrum family extension
assumptions: The initial functions are nontrivial s-plateaued Boolean functions on F_2^n
Their Walsh spectra are pairwise disjoint
The initial family has r<2^s members
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later paper proves extension for every admissible partial family or gives a counterexample; constructions of selected complete families do not settle arbitrary extendability.
